records.name: A. Overholt Straight Rye
records.quality_anchor_comparison: Soft fruit and browned-butter sweetness balance rye spice successfully. The evidence supports good execution with modest complexity rather than exceptional concentration.

quality_calibration_details.limitations: Exact reviewed bottle or edition only; no blind panel or whole-program consensus is claimed.

records.name: Ancient Age
records.quality_anchor_comparison: Below the Maker’s/Bulleit 5.0 midpoint because thin texture and a short finish recur across three independent accounts. It remains recognizably pleasant bourbon rather than the severe defects of the Cleveland 1.0 anchor. Its low price does not raise Quality.

quality_calibration_details.limitations: Identified expression or historical release; published ratings are not averaged. No claim of blind head-to-head consensus.

records.name: Ancient Age Preferred
records.quality_anchor_comparison: A provisional below-average blend assessment. One detailed critic finds little coherent flavor and medicinal alcohol; a substantive community account instead finds moderate body and a longer sweet finish. Sparse flavor development and disagreement prevent either catastrophic-floor status or ordinary competence. Universal calibration fits the neutral-spirit-heavy intended blend.

quality_calibration_details.limitations: One detailed critic and one substantive independent community account, materially divergent. Label-supported blend identity is corrected; neutral spirits are not themselves a defect, and older reviews do not establish a current blind consensus.

records.name: Ancient Ancient Age 10 Star
records.quality_anchor_comparison: Bourbon Obsessed enjoys a light apple-and-caramel profile; Bourbon Culture finds grain, ethanol and underdeveloped texture. Slightly below the ordinary midpoint fits that disagreement, safely above Cleveland’s severe defects. The name ten star is not an authenticated ten-year age statement.

quality_calibration_details.limitations: Existing dossier evidence and identity qualifications remain applicable.

records.name: Anderson’s Belle — Prohibition Collection 2 (2025)
records.quality_anchor_comparison: Pleasant definition and balance support a good 6.3 above the 5.0 bourbon midpoint. Texture and finish reservations prevent very-good or elite placement.

quality_calibration_details.limitations: Three independent publishers, but two brief media-event narratives. Confidence is medium, not a multi-bottle consensus.

records.name: Angel's Envy 10-Year Cask Strength Rye (2026)

quality_calibration_details.limitations: Exact reviewed bottle or edition only; no blind panel or whole-program consensus is claimed.

records.name: Angel's Envy Finished Rye
records.quality_anchor_comparison: A coherent dessert-like sweet-spicy profile fulfills its intended style successfully. Sweetness limits subtle development, but is not itself treated as a defect or a departure from rye requirements.

quality_calibration_details.limitations: Exact reviewed bottle or edition only; no blind panel or whole-program consensus is claimed.

records.name: Angel's Envy Finished Rye (2015)

quality_calibration_details.limitations: Exact reviewed bottle or edition only; no blind panel or whole-program consensus is claimed.

records.name: Angel’s Envy 2024 Cask Strength Bourbon

quality_calibration_details.limitations: Exact reviewed bottle or edition only; no blind panel or whole-program consensus is claimed.

records.name: Angel’s Envy Bottled in Bond Cask Strength Bourbon
records.quality_anchor_comparison: The two matched accounts disagree materially: one finds a narrow, dry and short profile, while the other finds developed fruit and a moderately long close. A cautious good-execution estimate credits the richer account without ignoring the weaker one. This is one June 2024 release, not two distinct editions.

quality_calibration_details.limitations: Exact reviewed bottle or edition only; no blind panel or whole-program consensus is claimed.

records.name: Angel’s Envy Bourbon Port Finish

quality_calibration_details.limitations: Exact reviewed bottle or edition only; no blind panel or whole-program consensus is claimed.

records.name: Angel’s Envy Cask Strength Bourbon 10 Year — 2025, batch C14

quality_calibration_details.limitations: Exact reviewed bottle or edition only; no blind panel or whole-program consensus is claimed.

records.name: Angel’s Envy Cask Strength Bourbon — 15th edition (2026)
records.quality_confidence: Medium: several dated, matched independent firsthand accounts
records.quality_anchor_comparison: Two matching 2026 reviews independently describe rich fruit, textural depth and effective proof integration; Drinkhacker finds more oak dryness than ideal. At 8.1 this is excellent bourbon, not reference-class because the tannin interferes with the finish.

quality_calibration_details.limitations: Exact reviewed bottle or edition only; no blind panel or whole-program consensus is claimed.

records.name: Angel’s Envy Cask Strength Rye — inaugural edition (2023)
records.quality_anchor_comparison: Five exact-edition independent accounts agree this 2023 114.4-proof rye succeeds at integrating substantial rye spice with Sauternes sweetness and toasted-oak structure. Paste stresses rye-grain intensity and impressive heat control; The Whiskey Wash notes a creamier and dessert-like profile; InsideHook finds a drier, more herbal character. The editorial 8.5 is an excellent rye judgement calibrated below the 10/10 Redemption Ancients 18-year 2017 rye anchor, not a conversion of reviewers’ different numeric scales.

quality_calibration_details.limitations: Exact named release; independent publications, no personal tasting or blind tasting claimed

records.name: Belle Meade Straight Bourbon

records.name: Benchmark Bonded
records.quality_anchor_comparison: Breaking Bourbon, the Whiskey Shelf and Bourbon Obsessed find a fuller sweet-spice profile than the weakest Benchmark bottles, while retaining some youthful grain and limited finish. The result clears the Maker’s/Bulleit midpoint and approaches the useful Very Old Barton 100 tier. Bonded status supplies identity and a minimum age, not automatic quality points.

quality_calibration_details.limitations: Existing dossier evidence and identity qualifications remain applicable.

records.name: Benchmark Full Proof
records.quality_anchor_comparison: The matched reviews describe stronger caramel, fruit and spice, but also heat and a finish that does not develop as far as the proof suggests. That supports good bourbon, above the ordinary midpoint and below the better integrated Weller Full Proof. The small lead over Bonded is about presence, not a linear proof rule.

quality_calibration_details.limitations: Existing dossier evidence and identity qualifications remain applicable.

records.name: Benchmark Old No. 8 Bourbon
records.quality_anchor_comparison: Breaking Bourbon finds muted flavor and a short, one-dimensional close; the Whiskey Shelf adds harsh grain and bitter dryness, while Bourbon & Banter supplies a genuine budget-positive counterpoint. That leaves Benchmark below the Maker’s/Bulleit midpoint, but well above Cleveland’s persistent chemical defects. Its recognizable sweetness prevents a poor-end score; Cabin Still is similarly limited, with less reported harshness.

quality_calibration_details.limitations: Existing dossier evidence and identity qualifications remain applicable.

records.name: Benchmark Rye (2026)
records.quality_anchor_comparison: A provisional competent-to-good rye estimate: fruit, caramel and spice cohere, but slight thinness and moderate development limit the ceiling. The incomplete native Rye floor is not used to create a new falsely established native score; parent execution anchors underlie this one-source assessment.

quality_calibration_details.limitations: One substantive independent critic; the reviewed $18 price is separate from the retained NC $15.95. Rye native endpoints remain unchanged and provisional.

records.name: Benchmark Single Barrel
records.quality_anchor_comparison: Four publishers supply barrel-level evidence of caramel, fruit and spice with a more approachable delivery than Full Proof. The samples vary in polish and finish, so a good-category position is better supported than a premium single-barrel ranking. It remains above No. 8 and below the richer Blanton’s samples.

quality_calibration_details.limitations: Different critics tasted different barrels. The score describes the reviewed range, not a guarantee for every barrel.

records.name: Benchmark Small Batch
records.quality_anchor_comparison: The three matched publishers describe a recognizable caramel-and-fruit bourbon with a modest body and a fairly short ending. It sits near the ordinary bourbon midpoint, slightly above Top Floor’s lighter delivery. The evidence does not support treating the words small batch as a complexity guarantee.

quality_calibration_details.limitations: Existing dossier evidence and identity qualifications remain applicable.

records.name: Benchmark Top Floor
records.quality_anchor_comparison: Breaking Bourbon finds a simple sweet profile and limited finish; the Whiskey Shelf and Bourbon Obsessed add usable fruit and spice rather than persistent defects. This fits the Maker’s/Bulleit ordinary midpoint. It is a clear step above No. 8’s recurring thin grain and bitterness, without the depth of Wild Turkey 101.

quality_calibration_details.limitations: Existing dossier evidence and identity qualifications remain applicable.

records.name: Blanton’s Gold Edition
records.quality_anchor_comparison: Breaking Bourbon’s historical barrel is richer and longer than Original, but the 2026 Barrel Banter voices disagree: one enjoys oily fruit and a long close, another finds approachable sweetness with limited depth. This supports very good bourbon with constrained confidence, below consistently richer Weller Full Proof and far below the selected ceiling.

quality_calibration_details.limitations: Breaking Bourbon reviewed a 2012 international barrel; Barrel Banter reviewed later bottles. Two voices within Barrel Banter count as one publisher. The score is limited to this variable standard-strength range.

records.name: Blanton’s Original Single Barrel
records.quality_anchor_comparison: Breaking Bourbon, the Whiskey Shelf and Bourbon Obsessed converge on an approachable fruit, caramel and spice profile, while finding limits to depth and persistence. This is clearly above the ordinary bourbon midpoint and near Maker’s 46, rather than near the category ceiling. Individual barrel variation remains material.

quality_calibration_details.limitations: The reviews cover different standard barrels. No single barrel is authenticated by this program-level score.

records.name: Blanton’s Special Reserve
records.quality_anchor_comparison: Breaking Bourbon finds watery delivery and a finish vulnerable to dilution; Bourbon Culture is more positive about the fruit while still finding the result underwhelming. Slightly below the Maker’s/Bulleit ordinary midpoint is supported; this is not the defect-heavy poor end of bourbon.

quality_calibration_details.limitations: Existing dossier evidence and identity qualifications remain applicable.

records.name: Blanton’s Straight from the Barrel
records.quality_anchor_comparison: Three publishers find more weight and concentration than the diluted Blanton’s variants, with meaningful disagreements about one-dimensional sweetness, heat and dry oak. Very good bourbon fits the reviewed barrels, near Weller Full Proof but below the best integrated annual BTAC releases. No universal proof or barrel verdict is implied.

quality_calibration_details.limitations: Proof and barrel identity vary. The NC row is a program price, not a match to every review sample.

records.name: Blaum Bros Straight Bourbon — 2019–20 era
records.quality_anchor_comparison: The 2019–20 evidence spans Whiskeyfellow’s oily texture and lingering spice, Bourbon & Banter’s enjoyable but simple profile, and Breaking Bourbon’s obstructive youthful grain. These specific early releases sit just above ordinary bourbon, rather than at the excellent end of craft production. The positive texture evidence places them ahead of Benchmark and near Larceny; uneven development keeps them far from Michter’s 2024 ceiling.

quality_calibration_details.limitations: Existing dossier evidence and identity qualifications remain applicable.

records.name: Old Rip Van Winkle 10 Year
records.quality_confidence: Low–medium; recurring expression, acknowledged vintage variation
records.quality_anchor_comparison: Quality 7.5§ places the recurring modern expression firmly above the ordinary 5.0 Maker’s/Bulleit anchors and the 6.2 Old Grand-Dad 114 reference. Concentrated fruit, texture and an integrated lingering close support very good execution. The limited breadth and variable dryness keep it below the consistently excellent development needed for an 8.0. Weller 12 at 7.2 is a nearby wheated reference; Maker’s Cellar Aged 2024 at 8.4 illustrates the next level without donating its score.

quality_calibration_details.material_comparability: Recurring modern Old Rip Van Winkle 10 Year: identified release years 2021, 2022, 2023; 107 proof, 10 years, comparable disclosed grain/style. This provisional expression-level judgment is not a score for an unidentified 2025 or 2026 bottling. Known legacy formulations and materially different strengths are excluded.
quality_calibration_details.major_dissent: Amongst finds limited breadth despite enjoyment; Whiskey Jar prefers the 2022 ten-year to that year’s Pappy 15; the 2023 community account finds a drier ending. No older Stitzel-Weller bottle supplies this score.

records.name: Old Stagg — Prohibition Collection 1 (2023)
records.quality_anchor_comparison: Very good balance and mature wood/fruit development are supported despite a dry, heat-driven close. The exact 132.4-proof 2023 component is identifiable; uncertainty over the statutory grain category is not itself a reason to withhold Quality. Universal scoring avoids choosing incompatible native anchors.

quality_calibration_details.limitations: Three independent publishers; statutory category remains explicitly unconfirmed. Dry wood and heat are limits, not laboratory defects. Value requires an actual component price.

records.name: Pappy Van Winkle’s Family Reserve 15 Year
records.quality_confidence: Low–medium; recurring expression, acknowledged vintage variation
records.quality_anchor_comparison: Quality 7.6§ rewards recurring mature fruit, texture and coherent spice above the ordinary 5.0 anchors and the 6.2 OGD 114 reference. Some matched bottles show excellent or better execution, but the uneven middle and finishing depth prevent transferring that peak to the whole expression. It sits below Maker’s Cellar Aged 2024 at 8.4 and near the very-good mature-bourbon tier. Age, portrait and scarcity contribute no points.

quality_calibration_details.material_comparability: Recurring modern Pappy Van Winkle’s Family Reserve 15 Year: identified release years 2019, 2021, 2022, 2024; 107 proof, 15 years, comparable disclosed grain/style. This provisional expression-level judgment is not a score for an unidentified 2025 or 2026 bottling. Known legacy formulations and materially different strengths are excluded.
quality_calibration_details.major_dissent: The strongly positive 2019 bottle does not stand for every later release. The 2021 review is less impressed, Whiskey Jar prefers Old Rip in its 2022 comparison, and the 2024 small pour has a weak ending. A positive 2022 community glass adds another useful but nonrepresentative voice.

records.name: Pappy Van Winkle’s Family Reserve 20 Year
records.quality_confidence: Low–medium; recurring expression, acknowledged vintage variation
records.quality_anchor_comparison: Quality 7.8§ lies near excellent execution: the stronger modern accounts show balanced old wood, developed fruit and rewarding texture above the ordinary 5.0 Bourbon anchors. The uneven finish and the less concentrated 2024 report keep the expression below a confident 8.0. Knob Creek 18 Year 2022 at 8.0 and Maker’s Cellar Aged 2024 at 8.4 provide nearby execution tests; the 10.0 Michter’s twenty-year anchor requires much more complete performance.

quality_calibration_details.material_comparability: Recurring modern Pappy Van Winkle’s Family Reserve 20 Year: identified release years 2019, 2021, 2022, 2024; 90.4 proof, 20 years, comparable disclosed grain/style. quality_calibration_details.major_dissent: UPROXX’s enthusiastic 2021 and 2022 accounts are one publisher, not two independent critics. Bourbon Culture finds the 2019 finish comparatively weak, and the 2024 community report is initially underwhelmed. Earlier Stitzel-Weller bottles, including the explicitly 2008 legacy review, do not set this score.

records.name: Pappy Van Winkle’s Family Reserve 23 Year
records.quality_anchor_comparison: Quality 7.2§ rewards the richer aroma, mature development and sweetness that often prevents wood from becoming wholly unpleasant. It remains above the ordinary 5.0 anchors but below Knob Creek 18 Year 2022 at 8.0 and the more complete aged wheated benchmark, Maker’s Cellar Aged 2024 at 8.4. Repeated palate dominance and a dry, less rewarding finish prevent age or a few excellent aromas from establishing excellent overall execution. Confidence is low because the stock provenance is not fully documented.

quality_calibration_details.material_comparability: Recurring modern Pappy Van Winkle’s Family Reserve 23 Year: identified release years 2019, 2021, 2022; 95.6 proof, 23 years, comparable disclosed grain/style. This provisional expression-level judgment is not a score for an unidentified 2025 or 2026 bottling. Component provenance is uncertain; continuity is inferred from the stable commercial identity and no authenticated formulation break within this cohort.
quality_calibration_details.major_dissent: The 2021 individual account enjoys the richness; Whiskey Consensus and Bourbon Culture identify limits beneath positive verdicts; UPROXX dislikes the dry bitterness. Stock-origin claims for modern bottles conflict and are unconfirmed. The provisional pool assumes comparable commercial age/proof/wheated style across 2019–2022, not proven identical distillery components. Known earlier Stitzel-Weller and Old Boone bottles are excluded, and a documented formulation break would require splitting this cohort.
